title: Twelve Days to Kickoff. The NRI's Complete Guide to the 2026 FIFA World Cup in America.
excerpt: Forty-eight teams. Eleven American cities. Messi and Ronaldo's last World Cup. India is not playing but the diaspora has never been closer to the biggest tournament on earth. Here is everything you need to know.
body:
The 2026 FIFA World Cup kicks off on June 11 in Mexico City. For the first time in history, the tournament is spread across three countries — the United States, Canada, and Mexico. Forty-eight teams. Eighty matches. Eleven American cities. And for the Indian diaspora in North America, the biggest sporting event in the world is, for once, playing in their time zone.

India is not in the tournament. That has not changed. But this World Cup is different from every one before it. It is happening where NRIs live, work, and commute. Some of the world's most iconic stadiums — MetLife, SoFi, AT&T — will host group stage matches you can drive to on a weeknight. This is the NRI viewer's complete guide.

## The Schedule: Key Dates

The group stage runs from June 11 to June 27. The round of 32 — an expanded format new to this World Cup — begins June 28. The final is on July 19 at MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, New Jersey.

For the first time, 48 teams have been divided into 12 groups of four. The top two from each group advance, along with the eight best third-place finishers. That means 32 of 48 teams make the knockouts — a format designed to keep almost every team alive until the final matchday.

## Where to Watch

In the United States, Fox and FS1 carry all 80 matches in English. Spanish-language coverage is on Telemundo and Peacock. In India, Zee Entertainment is close to finalizing broadcast rights after a last-minute scramble — the deal was not confirmed as of late May, leaving Indian viewers in suspense just two weeks before kickoff.

For NRIs in the US and Canada, the time-zone advantage is significant. Group stage matches typically kick off at 12 PM, 3 PM, 6 PM, and 9 PM Eastern. No 3:30 AM alarms. No bleary-eyed mornings. The World Cup, for once, is in your living room at a reasonable hour.

## The Groups You Should Care About

**Group D: United States vs Paraguay, Australia, Turkey** — The host nation opens at SoFi Stadium in Los Angeles on June 13. If you live in Southern California, tickets are available but going fast.

**Group F: Netherlands vs Japan, Sweden, Tunisia** — Japan's presence means NRI communities across North America will find a natural rooting interest. Japan played some of the most exciting football at the 2022 World Cup in Qatar and will look to go further.

**Group J: Argentina vs Algeria, Austria, Jordan** — Messi. That is the entire reason. The 39-year-old is almost certainly playing his final World Cup. He has been clear that this is it. The group stage matches in Houston and Miami will be pilgrimage events.

**Group K: Portugal vs DR Congo, Uzbekistan, Colombia** — Ronaldo at 41. Like Messi, this is likely his last World Cup. The two greatest players of their generation, on opposite sides of the bracket, both chasing one final moment.

## NRI Hotspot Venues

Seven of the eleven US host cities have among the largest Indian-American populations in the country:

- **New York/New Jersey (MetLife Stadium)** — Hosts the final on July 19. The tri-state area has the highest concentration of Indian Americans in the US. Group L matches (England vs Croatia vs Ghana vs Panama) play here.
- **San Francisco Bay Area (Levi's Stadium, Santa Clara)** — The Silicon Valley diaspora can watch a round of 32 match on July 1. Group stage not assigned to this venue, but knockout matches are.
- **Houston (NRG Stadium)** — Texas has one of the fastest-growing Indian populations. Group C and knockout matches play here.
- **Dallas (AT&T Stadium)** — Another Texas NRI hub. Round of 32 and round of 16 matches.
- **Atlanta (Mercedes-Benz Stadium)** — Growing desi community. Hosts a round of 32 match July 1.
- **Boston (Gillette Stadium)** — Large South Asian student and professional population. Five group stage matches including England vs Ghana on June 23.
- **Toronto (BMO Field)** — Canada's largest Indian community. Hosts a round of 32 match on July 2.

## What NRIs Are Actually Going to Watch

India's absence means there is no national team to rally around. But the diaspora has never lacked for football opinions. Here is what will drive viewership:

**Messi and Ronaldo's farewell.** This is the single biggest draw. An entire generation of NRIs grew up watching Messi-Ronaldo debates in school, on WhatsApp groups, and on Twitter. The 2026 World Cup is the closing chapter of that rivalry.

**Japan and South Korea.** Asian representation matters. Japanese football in particular has exploded in quality — three players now start for top European clubs — and the Samurai Blue will have a massive following among NRIs who root for Asian success on the global stage.

**England.** The Premier League is the most-watched football league in India and among NRIs. England's group matches — especially at Gillette Stadium in Boston — will draw large South Asian crowds.

**Community watch parties.** Indian-American cultural organizations in every major metro are already planning World Cup screening events. Check with your local desi community Facebook group or temple — the World Cup has a way of bringing out gatherings that cricket usually monopolizes.

## The Bottom Line

This World Cup is the most accessible global sporting event NRIs in North America have ever had. No midnight kickoffs. No scrambling for streams. No time-zone math. The matches are on network television, in stadiums you can reach by car, in cities where your community lives.

India may not be on the pitch. But the World Cup has never been closer to the Indian diaspora than it is right now. June 11 is twelve days away. Set your calendars.
author: Diaspora Desk
